subject: physical-education
title: Independent application A: targeted correction and the practice design that fixes it
focus: targeted correction and the practice design that fixes it
essentialQuestion: How do I find the flaw in my own movement without anyone filming me?
materials: equipment for the chosen skill or a substitute
privacySafeScenario: Choose one skill, identify its critical features, diagnose the learner’s own limiting feature from outcome evidence, design and run the corrective practice, and document the change.
studentTask: Learner applies targeted correction and the practice design that fixes it in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind targeted correction and the practice design that fixes it and name one adjustment for the next session.
completionCriteria: The learner completes or fully describes the targeted correction and the practice design that fixes it task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.
adaptationChoices: Any skill the learner can perform, in any range or position, is a valid choice, including a mobility-aid skill or a seated skill. Analysis may be described, drawn, or tabled.
extensionChallenge: Apply targeted correction and the practice design that fixes it under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Any skill the learner can perform, in any range or position, is a valid choice, including a mobility-aid skill or a seated skill. Analysis may be described, drawn, or tabled.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice or try one safe, optional example of targeted correction and the practice design that fixes it in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
